html:
The Ogaden War was fought from July 1977 to March 1978 when Somalia invaded the Ogaden, the Somali-inhabited east of Ethiopia, and was driven back.

Siad Barre struck while Ethiopia was in turmoil after the revolution, and Somali forces took most of the region and besieged the town of Jijiga and then Harar. Then the Soviet Union, until then Somalia's ally, switched to the Derg, and flew in weapons and advisers along with thousands of Cuban troops.

Ethiopia retook the Ogaden in early 1978. Hundreds of thousands of refugees fled into Somalia. Defeat weakened Siad Barre's rule and led to the rebellions that ended in the Somali civil war. It was one of the main Cold War conflicts in Africa.
sum: The Ogaden War was fought from July 1977 to March 1978 when Somalia invaded the Ogaden, the Somali-inhabited east of Ethiopia, and was driven back.
